classification: Retrospective pinned-source applicability audit; not a new bug reproduction or novel theoretical result

observations.observation: Deterministic selection sorts the drained, already completed results by task ID. It does not itself wait for globally earlier outstanding task IDs.
observations.limit: Source control-flow inference only. No distributed run, sampling-bias magnitude, capability effect or correctness violation is established.

observations.observation: The option documents ordering of completed results and restricts supported end-to-end determinism to zero head off-policyness. Its validation warns explicitly about nondeterministic task-to-weight-version mapping otherwise.
observations.limit: This is an acknowledged upstream contract, not a newly discovered scheduler bug.

observations.observation: The published orchestrator waits for subprocess sampling, execution, reward assignment and training sequentially, both initially and in each training iteration.
observations.limit: This entry point does not instantiate asynchronous feedback-version replacement during a coding trajectory. This says nothing about unpublished systems or separate agentic uses of the trained tester.

observations.observation: Coder and tester prompts are formed before the joint generation call; returned outputs are split into coder and tester samples.
observations.limit: Does not establish agent-visible, changing verifier observations within multi-turn training rollouts.

observations.observation: The code reward in this path uses the ground-truth-test slice. Tester rewards use the execution matrix and which codes passed those tests.
observations.limit: Do not describe this path as coder RL receiving a changing learned tester as its in-trajectory feedback.

observations.observation: CodingToolAgent stores its public_grader callback at construction and test_public awaits that callback. The training_turns adapter attaches the terminal reward and verifier version separately.
observations.limit: A mutable external callback is possible, but this source alone does not establish a learned public grader that changes during real distributed training.

prior_art_boundary.observation: Completion/length bias and asynchronous queue selection are already studied. Its queue-drop independence argument is an explicitly approximate steady-state argument.
prior_art_boundary.limit: No novelty claim for identifying length-biased completed-data selection.

prior_art_boundary.observation: Anytime Monte Carlo already studies wall-clock interruption and state-dependent computation-time bias.
prior_art_boundary.limit: No claim that a scheduler-dependence warning is a new probability theorem.

prior_art_boundary.observation: Nonstationary multiagent replay, importance sampling and replay fingerprints are established prior work.
prior_art_boundary.limit: Joint actor/verifier version tracking or a product of likelihood ratios alone does not establish a new method.
